text: Finance, Marketing, and the warehouse team each define Active Customer differently -- and every leadership report built on that term disagrees with the other two.

Finance counts anyone with a posted invoice in the last 12 months. Marketing counts anyone engaged with a campaign in the last 90 days. The warehouse just inherits whichever record landed most recently.

That's the key discovery: Finance's and Marketing's rules are both genuinely defensible. The warehouse's number isn't a third opinion at all -- it's an unintended side effect of load order nobody designed on purpose.
The approved definition combines both real signals into one rule, keyed to a single customer record of record, and gets published in Purview's glossary with a named steward and a verification query.
One trusted definition now replaces three. Next: deciding which of Veridian's data is sensitive enough to need a label.
